transcript: When anxiety enters your life, you are no longer quite the same person. Things that once felt normal begin to feel heavy. You no longer care about going out the way you used to. Your body begins sending strange signals. A numb arm, a racing heart, a mind that refuses to rest. Even leaving your own house can start to feel like a mountain. Some people only talk about anxiety when they board a plane, when the sky shakes and the mind searches for control. But imagine carrying that same feeling in the middle of a quiet grocery store. Nothing dangerous is happening, yet your body believes it is. Your breath shortens, your thoughts scatter, and suddenly the world that once felt familiar becomes overwhelming. I wrote about this moment in my book, The Way Back to Stillness, because many people believe they are broken, when in truth they are simply overwhelmed. I remember one of the worst moments of my life happening in the most ordinary place, a quiet post office. That is the strange thing about anxiety. It does not wait for dramatic moments. Sometimes it arrives in the middle of a normal day and quietly steals your peace. But peace can be learned again. If this message found you at the right time, the full book is in my bio.
